# ADR 0136: Editor Preview Asset Residency and Asynchronous Streaming

Status: Accepted
Date: 2026-08-17
Amends: ADR 0071, ADR 0104
Relates to: ADR 0068, ADR 0072, ADR 0075, ADR 0078, ADR 0117, ADR 0135

## Context

GameEngine already moved the source-import path for large model files off the
Editor UI thread. `AssetImportManager` performs model parsing and image decoding
on a background worker, and ADR 0075 deliberately serializes mutation-bearing
imports through one queued worker. That solved the case where adding or
reimporting a source directly froze the immediate-mode Editor.

The interactive preview path is different. A Scene View rebuild still performs
authoring-to-runtime conversion synchronously from `SceneView::show`. On a model
cache miss, conversion can reach the format-independent model importer and read,
parse, decode, and construct model data before the next UI frame. ADR 0071
reduced repeated glTF work by retaining parsed model and decoded texture data,
and ADR 0072 retains one preview world across unchanged frames. ADR 0104 also
requires GPU mesh uploads to survive a preview-world rebuild.

Those optimizations currently stop at a single `SceneView` instance. The
dedicated Animation Preview owns a separate `SceneView`, therefore a separate
source/decode cache, GPU mesh cache, preview world, and preview renderer. Other
preview surfaces can make the same choice. A character that is already visible
in the main Scene View can consequently become a cold asset again when
Animation Preview first opens. The first draw of a cold preview can additionally
initialize its `PreviewRenderer` synchronously from the immediate UI path.

This is the wrong lifetime boundary. Imported model identity belongs to the
project, GPU resource identity belongs to the active device and asset
generation, while a preview world belongs only to one view and its simulation
state. Conflating all three lifetimes inside `SceneView` produces duplicate CPU
work, duplicate GPU work, avoidable first-open stalls, and no single place to
apply streaming or memory-pressure policy.

ADR 0117 makes the ownership boundary explicit: one Editor process edits exactly
one project for its process lifetime. That project-scoped Editor workspace is
therefore the natural lifetime for reusable CPU asset residency. The active GPU
device is the natural lifetime for reusable GPU residency and preview pipeline
state. ADR 0135 may deliberately reclaim recreatable GPU resources for native
agent inference, so any new residency contract must also support explicit
eviction and correct reconstruction.

A project-wide decision is required for five related changes:

1. sharing asset caches across every Editor preview surface;
2. reusing successful background-import results instead of reparsing the source
   during preview conversion;
3. sharing GPU residency across preview worlds;
4. removing cold preview-renderer initialization from window-open/UI-frame
   latency; and
5. making cold asset materialization asynchronous with bounded GPU upload work.

## Decision

### 1. Reusable CPU asset residency is project-scoped, not `SceneView`-scoped

The Editor owns one project-scoped asset-residency service for the lifetime of
its `EditorWorkspace`. The concrete type name is not a public compatibility
contract; `ProjectAssetResidency` is used here as a conceptual name.

Every preview surface in that Editor process MUST obtain reusable immutable
asset data through the same residency service, including at minimum:

- the main Scene View;
- Animation Preview;
- material/model/asset previews that need imported model data;
- thumbnail or inspector previews that materialize the same assets; and
- future graph or debugging views that render project assets.

The service retains immutable, conversion-ready CPU results such as parsed
model/import results and decoded texture payloads. The representation after the
parser boundary remains format-independent according to ADR 0078. The Editor
MUST NOT create separate PMX, FBX, and glTF residency architectures merely
because the current ADR 0071 cache has a historical glTF-specific name.

A resident entry is identified by stable project asset identity plus an
in-memory **asset generation** representing the exact successful source/import
state that produced it. Generation invalidation MUST account for every input
that can change the conversion-ready result, including source/dependency
changes and import settings that affect model construction. Stable `AssetId`
values themselves do not change when a generation changes.

Multiple requests for the same asset generation MUST coalesce onto one
in-flight materialization. Two preview windows requesting the same cold model
must not launch two parsers.

Project close drops project CPU residency. A project switch is process
replacement under ADR 0117, so project residency is never silently rebound from
one project to another.

This amends ADR 0071 for the Editor: its shared parse/decode behavior remains
valid, but the owning lifetime is raised from one repeated-conversion host to
the project-scoped Editor residency service. `SharedGltfImportCache` MAY remain
as a lower-level compatibility helper for non-Editor hosts and during migration.

### 2. Successful background import publishes the conversion-ready result for preview reuse

The source import/reimport pipeline and preview materialization MUST converge on
the same immutable conversion-ready result.

After a background import succeeds, the Editor publishes that exact successful
result, or an immutable equivalent derived without reparsing source bytes, into
project residency before preview consumers request it. The publication is
atomic with respect to residency generation: a consumer observes either the
previous complete generation or the new complete generation, never a mixture of
old meshes with new materials, skeletons, clips, or decoded textures.

Conceptually:

```text
source file / dependencies
        |
        v
background read + parse + decode + model build
        |
        +------> import metadata / generated artifact persistence
        |
        v
project CPU residency (immutable generation)
        |
        +------> Scene View conversion
        +------> Animation Preview conversion
        +------> other preview consumers
```

The background importer MUST NOT discard a large conversion-ready model result
and force the Scene View to reconstruct the same result from the source a moment
later.

A cold Editor process may have valid persisted import metadata but no in-memory
resident model yet. In that case, the first preview request schedules a
read-only background materialization for the current asset generation and
publishes the result into the same residency service. It does not make the
immediate UI frame perform source parsing.

If the source or relevant import inputs change while work is in flight, the
completed stale result MUST be discarded rather than published under the new
generation. Reimport creates or advances the generation and atomically replaces
the resident result only after the new result is complete.

Mutation-bearing import jobs MAY remain serialized initially as ADR 0075
defines. This ADR does not require unlimited parallel imports. Worker count is a
scheduler policy; the hard requirement is that expensive source work is not
performed by the UI thread and duplicate requests for one generation are
deduplicated.

### 3. GPU asset residency is shared across preview worlds on the active device

GPU meshes, imported textures, and other immutable reusable GPU asset resources
MUST be reusable across all preview worlds that render the same current asset
generation on the same GPU device.

A preview world may keep world-local runtime handles or alias tables, but those
handles MUST resolve to shared device-resident buffers/textures rather than
causing a fresh upload merely because another `SceneView`, Animation Preview,
or thumbnail world was constructed.

The cache key MUST distinguish at least:

- GPU device generation/identity;
- asset or content identity; and
- the source/import generation whose immutable CPU data produced the upload.

Pointer identity MAY be an optimization when it is backed by the stronger
generation/content contract; pointer identity alone must not make stale GPU
content appear current.

`SharedGpuMeshCache` is the existing starting mechanism for mesh residency. The
Editor-level composition MUST share one compatible backing residency across its
preview surfaces instead of constructing one independent backing cache per
`SceneView`. Equivalent sharing is required for imported texture residency
where duplicate preview uploads can occur.

The following remain view-local and MUST NOT be shared merely to satisfy this
ADR:

- ECS/runtime preview worlds;
- animation graph state and preview time;
- particle or secondary-physics simulation state;
- selection, camera, and gizmo state;
- color/depth render targets whose size or lifetime belongs to one view; and
- other mutable per-preview state.

This preserves the isolation contract of ADR 0072. We share immutable expensive
asset residency, not the preview world itself.

GPU residency is recreatable. It is released on device loss/reset and project
shutdown, and it participates in ADR 0135 staged memory reclaim. An intentional
ADR 0135 eviction is allowed to cause a later re-upload; ordinary opening of a
second preview is not.

This further specifies ADR 0104's shared-GPU-cache requirement: "shared" means
shared across Editor preview surfaces for the applicable device/project
lifetime, not merely shared across rebuilds of one preview world.

### 4. Preview renderer initialization is device-lifetime preparation, not window-open work

Opening an Animation Preview or another preview window MUST NOT synchronously
perform cold renderer/pipeline initialization through an immediate-mode
`show`/draw call.

After the Editor obtains its GPU device, it owns device-scoped preview rendering
services. Expensive immutable renderer state such as shader modules, bind-group
layouts, render pipelines, samplers, and other device-wide preview
infrastructure SHOULD be created once and reused by every preview surface when
the renderer architecture permits it.

Initialization may occur during Editor bootstrap or as an explicit warm-up task
after the device is ready. The implementation does not have to make every GPU
API call execute on a background OS thread; it does have to remove synchronous
waiting for cold renderer construction from the user action that opens a
preview.

A view still owns its own size-dependent render targets and mutable render
state. This ADR does not require one globally mutable `PreviewRenderer` object
when doing so would create aliasing or state-coupling problems. The required
sharing boundary is the expensive immutable/device-scoped preparation.

If warm-up is not complete when a window opens, the Editor keeps the UI
interactive and shows a lightweight preparing state until the service is ready.
It MUST NOT use `pollster::block_on` or an equivalent unbounded wait inside the
preview's immediate UI path to hide that state.

Device reset invalidates prepared renderer services and schedules them for
reconstruction using the same non-blocking presentation behavior.

### 5. Cold preview loading is asynchronous and GPU uploads are frame-budgeted

Interactive Editor preview paths adopt an asynchronous materialization pipeline:

```text
request AssetId + generation
        |
        v
in-flight dedupe / priority scheduler
        |
        v
worker: file I/O -> parser -> image decode -> model build
        |
        v
project CPU residency
        |
        v
budgeted GPU upload queue
        |
        v
device GPU residency
        |
        v
preview world consumes ready handles
```

The following operations MUST NOT run synchronously as part of an ordinary
Editor UI-frame draw because a preview needs an asset:

- reading a large model source or dependency;
- parsing PMX, FBX, glTF/GLB, or another heavyweight model format;
- decoding imported images;
- rebuilding derived animation/model data whose cost scales with source size;
- waiting for cold preview-renderer initialization; or
- performing an unbounded batch of GPU uploads.

Small bounded metadata checks such as file stamps MAY remain synchronous when
measurement shows they are safe, but they MUST NOT become a path back to
whole-file reads or hashes.

File-backed data used only to populate preview UI, such as Animation Set
choices, SHOULD be retained by document/asset revision or loaded through the
same asynchronous/cached application layer rather than read and parsed from
disk every immediate-mode frame.

GPU uploads may need to execute through the render/device owner, but they are
scheduled under a per-frame budget. The implementation owns the concrete
budget units and adaptive policy; it SHOULD account for bytes, elapsed upload
time, and/or upload count rather than hard-coding one model-size threshold as
an architecture rule.

Upload/materialization priority is at least:

1. assets required by the currently visible, user-focused preview;
2. assets required by other visible previews;
3. speculative/warm-up work; and
4. thumbnails and background presentation.

A higher-priority request may move ahead of queued lower-priority work without
duplicating an already-running job. Cancellation and generation checks prevent
obsolete work from being published.

While a required asset is pending, the preview renders the last complete
generation when that is semantically safe, otherwise a placeholder/loading
state. The Editor remains interactive. Availability of a model is therefore an
asynchronous state, not permission to block the UI thread until the model is
ready.

## Cross-Cutting Invariants

The five decisions above are one contract and MUST preserve the following
invariants.

### Authoring and runtime boundaries

- Canonical project files remain the source of truth. Residency is derived,
  ephemeral application state.
- No Scene, prefab, graph, Animation Set, Material, project-settings, or asset
  manifest schema changes are introduced by this ADR.
- `StableId`, `AssetId`, `EntityId`, imported sub-asset IDs, and serialization
  rules do not change.
- Authoring transactions, undo/redo, Problems diagnostics, and best-effort
  conversion remain owned by their existing layers.
- Runtime/player/packaging hosts are not required to become asynchronous by
  this ADR. They may reuse lower-level residency primitives later, but Editor
  responsiveness must not weaken strict one-shot conversion semantics.

### Generation and last-good behavior

- A resident generation is immutable after publication.
- Reimport or relevant import-settings change produces a new generation rather
  than mutating a published generation in place.
- One preview build must not mix asset generations.
- An obsolete in-flight result is dropped if its requested generation is no
  longer current.
- Last-good rendering is permitted only from a complete prior generation and
  must be visibly replaced when the current generation becomes ready.
- A failed new generation preserves the prior complete generation for preview
  continuity when doing so does not misrepresent a deleted/unavailable asset;
  the failure remains visible through existing diagnostics.

### Ownership and memory pressure

- The project-scoped service owns CPU residency; preview windows borrow/share
  immutable entries.
- Device-scoped services own GPU residency and reusable renderer preparation.
- Preview worlds own mutable simulation state only.
- ADR 0135 may explicitly evict recreatable GPU residency. Reclaim does not
  invalidate canonical authoring state or CPU asset generation identity.
- The first implementation MAY retain CPU entries for the Editor project
  lifetime. A later measured LRU/size budget may evict cold CPU entries without
  changing this ADR as long as correctness and in-flight dedupe are preserved.

## Required Verification

Implementation of this ADR is not complete until the following behavior is
demonstrated.

1. **Scene View -> Animation Preview reuse.** With one imported model already
   fully resident and visible in the main Scene View, opening Animation Preview
   for that model performs no second source-file read/parse, image decode, or
   identical mesh/texture GPU upload. Constructing the isolated preview ECS
   world and its view-local render targets is allowed.
2. **Cold preview stays interactive.** Opening a preview for a cold large model
   leaves the Editor event/UI loop responsive while CPU materialization runs
   off-thread and GPU uploads respect the configured frame budget.
3. **Open/close reuse.** Closing and reopening a preview does not repeat cold
   model work unless the relevant generation was invalidated or residency was
   intentionally evicted.
4. **Atomic reimport replacement.** A reimport cannot expose mixed old/new
   meshes, materials, skeletons, clips, or textures to one preview build.
5. **In-flight dedupe.** Concurrent requests from at least two preview surfaces
   for the same cold generation execute one source materialization.
6. **Device/project cleanup.** Project shutdown releases project residency;
   device loss/reset invalidates device residency and renderer preparation; both
   can be reconstructed correctly.
7. **ADR 0135 recovery.** After deliberate aggressive GPU reclaim, returning to
   manual editing recreates evicted residency correctly and the re-upload is
   observable as intentional recovery rather than a normal preview duplicate.

Tests SHOULD use deterministic counters or instrumented loaders for source
materialization and upload counts rather than timing-only assertions.
Performance instrumentation SHOULD separately expose CPU materialization,
decode, queued GPU bytes, uploaded GPU bytes, and preview-ready latency so a
future regression can identify which stage returned to the UI path.

## Consequences

- Opening Animation Preview for a character already shown by Scene View no
  longer treats that character as a cold model merely because the preview owns
  a different runtime world.
- The first cold model still has real I/O, parsing, decoding, and upload cost,
  but that cost becomes asynchronous presentation state instead of one long UI
  frame.
- Reusing the background import result removes duplicated CPU work that a cache
  alone cannot avoid when the importer and preview own unrelated result
  lifetimes.
- Project/device residency intentionally retains more memory than
  per-window caches. This is the latency/memory tradeoff required for an editor;
  ADR 0135 provides an explicit aggressive GPU-reclaim path when memory is more
  valuable than resume latency.
- Asynchronous readiness introduces state that preview UI must represent:
  queued, materializing, CPU-ready, uploading, ready, failed, cancelled, and
  stale-generation outcomes. Those states must be observable rather than
  collapsed into a blocking call.
- Sharing immutable GPU resources reduces upload duplication but increases the
  importance of precise generation invalidation and device-loss handling.
- The design creates one place to add measured eviction, prefetch, or disk
  derived-artifact caching later without teaching every preview window its own
  policy.

## Alternatives Considered

### Keep one cache per `SceneView`

Rejected. It optimizes repeated frames in one view but directly preserves the
reported failure mode: a model warm in Scene View can be cold in Animation
Preview.

### Add more background threads but keep independent caches

Rejected as the architectural fix. Parallel duplicate work may reduce wall
clock time on some machines while increasing CPU, I/O, memory, and GPU
contention. Sharing and in-flight deduplication remove the work instead.

### Share only `SharedGpuMeshCache`

Rejected as incomplete. It avoids some duplicate mesh uploads while source
reads, model parsing, image decoding, texture uploads, and renderer cold-start
work can still stall or repeat.

### Share one runtime preview world between Scene View and Animation Preview

Rejected. Camera, selection, animation time, graph state, secondary physics,
particles, and other mutable preview state have different semantics. ADR 0072's
per-preview persistent world remains the correct isolation boundary.

### Eagerly load every project asset at Editor startup

Rejected. Large projects would trade an on-demand stall for excessive startup
time and memory residency. Residency is shared and demand-driven, with optional
low-priority warm-up.

### Make a disk-derived asset database mandatory in this ADR

Rejected for the first implementation. A content-addressed on-disk derived
artifact store can improve cold-process startup further, but it adds importer
versioning, artifact compatibility, cleanup, and storage policy. The in-memory
project/device residency and asynchronous materialization contract is required
whether or not that later cache exists.

### Define a fixed worker count or fixed MiB-per-frame upload limit

Rejected as an architecture contract. Hardware, model sizes, backend behavior,
and Editor workload differ. The contract is bounded, prioritized work with
measurement; exact scheduler limits are implementation policy.

## Compatibility and Migration

This ADR changes no persisted format and requires no project migration.

Implementation is staged in the same order as the five decisions:

1. introduce project-scoped CPU residency and inject it into every existing
   preview surface, initially adapting ADR 0071-compatible cached results;
2. publish successful background import/materialization results into that
   residency and make preview conversion consume them instead of reparsing;
3. lift mesh/texture GPU residency to the shared device/project preview
   composition and preserve per-world handles as aliases;
4. split device-scoped preview renderer preparation from per-view mutable
   render state and remove blocking cold initialization from preview `show`;
5. route cold materialization and GPU upload through the priority scheduler and
   enforce the per-frame upload budget/placeholder behavior.

The stages MAY ship in separate pull requests, but a partially completed
migration must not claim the verification guarantees of a later stage.

ADR 0071 remains an Accepted historical decision and a valid lower-level
repeated-conversion mechanism; this ADR amends the Editor ownership scope and
generalizes the result beyond one format-specific cache.

ADR 0072 remains authoritative for preview-world persistence and isolation.
This ADR deliberately does not share mutable runtime worlds.

ADR 0104 remains authoritative for Editor responsiveness. Its GPU-residency
decision is clarified to apply across Editor preview surfaces, not only rebuilds
of one Scene View.

ADR 0135 remains authoritative for native-agent GPU arbitration. Shared preview
GPU residency is considered recreatable persistent Editor state: retain it in
the normal path when budgets fit, and evict it only through explicit staged
reclaim when required.

Any implementation that changes an existing public Rust API, including
`GpuMeshCache` composition or model-import result publication, must update all
workspace callers and documentation in the same change according to the normal
breaking-change workflow. No public API shape is fixed by the conceptual names
used in this ADR.
